forefront: A tradition this serious about harm to the smallest insect — who examines the harm to the girl fasting for her family's standing?
healthy: Jainism has ~4–5 million adherents, mostly in India.
structure: Everyone audits everyone's austerity. Ask instead who audits the trusts, and how long the silence lasts.
law: State trust registrars over temple and community trusts, and the courts — which have already heard the minor-renunciation cases.
money: Public austerity events generate family status, and honor is the currency of that economy.
reach: Monastic authority over lay questions can discourage dissent on practices such as extreme fasting.
techniques: Thirty named techniques from domestic-abuse and social-psychology research, applied to institutions, in the eight stages of the cycle.
loops: The seven loops below show how the practices connect, so that each step makes the next one easier and the last step feeds the first.
say-do: The chair is held by trust boards, monastic acharyas and the marriage-and-credit network.
cost: Leaving costs marriage networks and business trust simultaneously — the community's commercial integration is the enforcement mechanism.
ledger: Trust boards and community elites control ritual honors and match networks, and families accrue status from members' austerities.
who-gets-hurt: They fall on women, on children, on families of modest means, on the elderly in contested santhara cases, and on anyone who dissents.
tiers: The table sets out what each role does, what it sees, what it is asked to do and what it could refuse.
voices: He was the petitioner who challenged santhara in court.
questions: If a child's fast brings the family status, ask honestly whose fast it is.
